hypothesis.observedProblem: runAgentLoop directly coordinates each optional capability in several places: it normalizes flags, chooses tools, mutates tools after MCP/A2A admission, composes instructions, and carries separate delegation counters into every tool call. This makes the core model/tool loop feature-aware and increases the chance that a new optional capability changes default or phase behavior.
hypothesis.suspectedCause: Capability policy and episode setup are interleaved with the transport loop instead of being represented as one phase-scoped plan. The loop therefore owns both orchestration mechanics and capability-specific admission/composition decisions.
hypothesis.proposedMutation: Add one loop-ext capability-plan module that creates the normalized episode capability state, composes instructions, builds the initial tool list, and applies admitted MCP/A2A tools. Use that plan from loop.ts while leaving execution, authority checks, counters, tracing, and all existing feature implementations unchanged.
hypothesis.expectedBenefit: The core loop will consume a single capability plan for instructions/tools and will no longer repeat feature-flag composition logic; default behavior, phase gating, tool admission, and delegation authority remain explicit and testable in one bounded module.
expectedRisks: A refactor of initialization/composition could accidentally expose an optional tool in repair or review phases.
Moving instruction/tool composition could alter exact prompt or tool ordering and break snapshot-style harness expectations.
The plan may hide capability state enough to make future tracing or counter updates less obvious.
